It carries a rich cultural history and tales of strong and brave women. For instance, in Slovakian folklore, St. Lucy is known as ‘Sv. Lučka’. She is believed to have brought light to the people of Syracuse during a famine, and is now celebrated as a symbol of light and hope.

historical_references.reference: In medieval Poland, a popular legend tells the story of Princess Ludmila of Bohemia, who was martyred around 921 AD. The Polish people are said to have hailed a child born to a noble family, named Lucinka, as a reincarnation of Saint Ludmila. This name became popular in Poland and was given to numerous girls throughout the Middle Ages.

The name Lucinka is also mentioned in the works of Polish poet Jan Kochanowski (1596-1629), particularly in his epic poem 'The Ghost of Helena'. In this work, the character Lucinka represents the ideal of chaste and virtuous womanhood. She is described as a symbol of hope and renewal in the face of grief and despair.
